text.p: SME - Parliament on Tuesday approved to the second reading a draft law on direct presidential elections. The law was worked out by the opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL).

- Police officers plan to organise a demonstration on Friday against lower-than-promised salary increase. Police say they were promised a 15 percent pay hike but that the finance ministry cut the increase to seven percent.

- The government on Tuesday asked President Michal Kovac to return to parliament for revision a law banning privatisation of the official Slovak Television second terrestrial channel. The president must return a law to the parliament if asked by the government to do so.
- The government on Tuesday dismissed the police chief, Jozef Dolgos.

NARODNA OBRODA - The National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, included some companies that have already gone bankrupt in the list of shares on offer for exchange for privatisation bonds.
- Parliament is expected to discuss a law regulating salary increases at its current session.

- Only 4,838 privatisation bonds changed hands in anonymous auctions since the beginning of this year, compared with 256,000 bonds matched in direct trades. The overall volume of bonds on offer in anonymous auctions total some 40,000.
- Local traders expect the banking sector to end the current two-week minimum reserves requirement period with better liquidity than the previous four periods.
PRAVDA - The controversial history book, which denies the persecution of Slovak Jews during World War Two, criticised by the European Union, will be withdrawn from schools.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The interior ministry has introduced a new measure on "suspicious financial operations" aimed against money laundering.

- Slovakia plans to build a complete motorway connection linking the Hungarian, Austrian and Polish borders by the year 2000. The highway corridor will be a part of the transeuropean connection between Baltic and Adriatic seas.
